svg.title: 3. Pilot light for server fleets with Elastic Disaster Recovery
svg.text: Pilot light for 40 servers with AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery: data replicates all the time, compute launches only when you need it
every 10 min for the last hour,
launch from latest or any point in time
failback: replicate changes made during the disaster back to the source, then cut over in a quiet hour
A full copy of the 40 servers
Data layer live in the recovery Region: Aurora Global Database secondary (headless or one small instance), DynamoDB global table replica, S3 replication.
Compute switched off: AMIs and container images replicated, Auto Scaling groups at desired = 0, EKS node groups at zero, Lambda functions deployed.
Recovery: promote the database, scale compute from 0 to production size, flip DNS or routing controls. The slowest step is usually waiting for capacity.
Pre-check: service quotas and On-Demand Capacity Reservations for the instance types you will need in the recovery Region.
